review_note: Reviewed line by line. (1) Oracle: dense Laplace marginal in base R (sb26_laplace, sb26_deriv_poisson/nb2) on observed rows only, with kernels built by hand: cov2cor(ape::vcv(tree)) on a height-3 tree, and exp(-d/median)+1e-6 I from shuffled coordinates. The package helpers are compared with independent constructions (b26sa_check_phylo_cov against ape::vcv, tolerance 1e-8; solve(drm_spatial_coords_precision) against the hand kernel, 1e-8). logLik agreement is 1e-5, and the fits agreed to well below that. (2) Bug sensitivity asserted above a floor of 0.5. My Totoro rerun with B29_PRINT showed gaps for NA-as-observed-zero 101-616, reversed SD 20-226, kernel-by-position 12-53, reversed site SD 16-46 and wrong kernel scale 0.75-14, so the smallest gap (0.75) is about 7e4 times the 1e-5 tolerance. (3) Rows fitted: Poisson and NB2 phylo_intercept, spatial_coordinate_intercept, phylo_numeric_slope and spatial_coordinate_slope, each with missing='include' and a predictor-dependent sd(). The simultaneous_iid_structured pair is phylo(1|id) + (1|site) with sd(id, level='phylogenetic') ~ z and sd(site) ~ z_site, a crossed design that matches the existing b26sa pair convention. The slope rows are slope-only phylo(0 + x | id) and spatial(0 + x | id), so they support the slope-member SD only, not an intercept-plus-slope structured pair. All 10 linked row_keys exist in the ledger. (4) All 8 manifest sha256 values, plus the log, manifest and test hashes, match current files. The console log shows 164 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped; ape was installed and the tests ran. Totoro run only, with the engine not exercised for Julia, which is correct for native rows.
